description:
FOUND s508 (Fable, 2026-10-05) by the review probes for s507c PART ONE; PRE-EXISTING on main fee16466.  Sibling of #2492 (the same two lines before an UNCAUGHT die under `pcl -e`); this is the CAUGHT case in an ordinary script file, where the program then continues correctly with noise on STDERR.

REPRODUCER (probes mod-die-eval, mod-req-eval-run in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s508/review/ph.pl (IMPL TAG [REGEX]; answers in out/ph.perl / ph.base / ph.tree; perl 5.40.3, main fee16466, the s507c tree 0229e0ec)):
  D.pm:   package D; die "D died\n"; 1;
  p.pl:   use lib "."; print "run1\n"; eval { require D }; print "caught: $@"; print "run2\n";
  perl:   run1 / caught: D died / Compilation failed in require at p.pl line 1. / run2          STDERR empty
  PCL:    run1 / caught: D died / run2                                                          STDERR: While evaluating the form starting at line 48, column 0
                                                                                                        of #P"/home/.../.pcl-cache/modules/33BD219452131DE9.lisp":
  Run 2 prints it again: a module whose load dies is never stored compiled, so it is loaded from TEXT every time.

CAUSE (known from #2492, not re-measured here): SBCL's source `load` prints that context from a handler the moment a serious condition is SIGNALLED inside a top-level form, before any handler further out (PCL's `eval`) decides to catch it.  A compiled (fasl) load prints nothing, which is why a healthy module never shows it.

WHY IT MATTERS: the USER's rule is that errors are tidy (one line, never Lisp text); `eval { require Some::Module; 1 } or fallback()` is the standard optional-dependency idiom, and a module that exists but refuses to load (wrong version, missing prerequisite, an XS half that is absent) is the case where it prints.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): load the cached module text through the runtime's own read-eval loop (or with SBCL's context printer rebound) for the DYING-module path only, and time a healthy module's first load before / after -- #2492 measured that loading everything as text is far too slow, so the fix must not change which modules load compiled.

ALSO SEEN, text only (not a goal by the USER's ruling, recorded so nobody re-derives it): perl appends "Compilation failed in require at FILE line N." to $@ for a module that dies during require; PCL's $@ is the module's message alone.
subject: A die inside a module that is being loaded prints two stray SBCL lines on STDERR -- `While evaluating the form starting at line N, column 0 of #P".../.pcl-cache/modules/....lisp":` -- even when the die is CAUGHT (`eval { require Optional::Module }` on a module whose load dies), on every run
